title: Forecasting Students' Success To Graduate Using Predictive Analytics
authors: Almonteros, J.; Matias, J.; Pitao, J.
venue: International Journal of Computing and Digital Systems
tldr: Genetic Algorithm feature selection with Logistic Regression achieves the highest accuracy and AUC for predicting student graduation on time using demographic and academic data.
problem_and_motivation: Universities need to predict which students will fail to graduate on time so early interventions can be made, but admission scores alone are insufficient predictors.
approach: Dataset of 2,207 new entrants from Caraga State University with 24 features covering demographics, academic records, and admission scores was collected and preprocessed.
KNN imputation handled missing numerical values while mode imputation filled missing categorical values, and binary encoding converted nominal features to 64 total predictors.
Three feature selection methods were tested separately: LASSO Regression (L1), Ridge Regression (L2), and Genetic Algorithm, each producing a distinct reduced feature set.
Seven classifiers were evaluated on each feature-selected dataset: Decision Tree, Random Forest, Ensemble, KNN, Logistic Regression, SVM, and Naive Bayes.
A 70-30 train-test split was used, and models were compared using accuracy and AUC score as primary evaluation metrics.
The best-performing model was deployed as a web-based application using Django Framework with individual and bulk CSV prediction capabilities.
findings: num: GA with Logistic Regression achieved 79% accuracy and 71% AUC, the highest among all classifier and feature selection combinations.
num: LASSO (L1) selected only 5 features and produced the lowest accuracy (58%) with Decision Tree and lowest AUC (50%).
num: GA showed a 21% increase in AUC for Logistic Regression compared to the no-feature-selected dataset with the same classifier.
num: NFS with Random Forest achieved 78% accuracy and 67% AUC, outperforming L1 and L2 but not GA-selected models.
num: Admission result was the most frequently selected feature across all 9 selection methods (6 of 9 times selected).
GA feature selection improved accuracy of every classifier compared to NFS, with gains ranging from 1% (Random Forest) to 10% (Logistic Regression).
Abstract score was the least selected feature across all methods, indicating it has minimal predictive power for graduation outcomes.
Mother income and sex were consistently selected alongside GPA and admission scores, suggesting demographic and socioeconomic factors matter.
key_figures_tables: Figure 2: Selected Features of the FS and Classifiers showing frequency of each feature across selection methods → Admission result and sex most consistently selected.
Table V: Evaluation metric scores across all classifier and feature selection combinations → GA consistently outperforms NFS, L1, and L2.
Table VI: Binary features selected by L1, L2, and GA across seven classifiers → GA selects 23-37 features while L1 selects only 5.

definitions.definition: Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, a L1 regularization method that shrinks coefficients to zero for feature selection.
A L2 regularization method that shrinks coefficients but does not reduce them to zero, unlike LASSO.
A wrapper feature selection method inspired by natural selection that iteratively evolves feature subsets through crossover and mutation.
Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve, a threshold-independent metric for evaluating classifier performance.
K-Nearest Neighbors, an imputation method that estimates missing values using the mean of the k nearest observations.
No Feature Selection, the baseline dataset containing all 64 features after binary encoding.
Support Vector Machine, a classifier that finds the optimal decision boundary separating classes using support vectors.
Senior High School, referring to the pre-college education stage in the Philippine K-12 curriculum.
Grade Point Average, a numerical measure of academic performance.
National Student Admission Examination, the standardized entrance exam used at Caraga State University.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a systematic comparison of three feature selection methods (LASSO, Ridge, Genetic Algorithm) combined with seven machine learning classifiers for predicting student graduation outcomes.
directly_justifies: GA with Logistic Regression achieves 79% accuracy and 71% AUC, outperforming all other combinations.
GA increases AUC by 21% for Logistic Regression compared to no feature selection.
Admission result is the most frequently selected feature across all selection methods.
LASSO selects only 5 features and produces the lowest overall performance.
Random Forest without feature selection achieves 78% accuracy, second highest overall.
limits: The study uses a single institutional dataset from Caraga State University, limiting generalizability to other universities or contexts.
The dataset contains significant missing values, particularly SHS track with 1,702 missing entries, which may affect imputation reliability.
No cross-validation was performed; a single 70-30 train-test split was used, which may produce unstable performance estimates.

limitations: The dataset from a single Philippine university limits generalizability to other institutional contexts.
SHS track has 1,702 missing values out of 2,207 samples, making imputation results questionable for that feature.
Only a single 70-30 train-test split was used without cross-validation, reducing result reliability.
remember_this: GA feature selection with Logistic Regression achieved the best performance at 79% accuracy and 71% AUC.
GA increased Logistic Regression AUC by 21% compared to no feature selection on the same classifier.
Admission result is the most predictive feature, selected in 6 of 9 selection methods.
LASSO (L1) was the weakest feature selector, selecting only 5 features and yielding 58% accuracy.
The model was deployed as a Django web application for bulk and individual student graduation prediction.
